description: Builds the §10.7 push path: relays store signed push registrations and send a wake signal through APNs, FCM and WebPush when a message arrives for a registered routing ID, and devices accept the wake, connect, and pull pending envelopes. The keri workstream owns the one function that checks a registration's signature against the identity's key state (§10.7.1 step 3); this PRD owns that function's interface, the relay code that calls it, and the error mapping (PUSH-005). Until keri replaces the stub body, every relay with push enabled answers 5003 and accepts no registration. PUSH-001 to PUSH-003 amend the specs and ADRs first, so each code story cites a section that already states its requirement. Alec ruled on 2026-10-12 that a registration lists routing IDs in place of plaintext context IDs (D5), that the registration key includes the device token so that each device registers separately (D6), and that WebPush is specified fully in a later gate (D3), which gate-push-webpush holds (PUSH-021 to PUSH-024).

stories.title: Amend the push payload and the device receipt rule per platform
stories.description:
Step 5 of §10.7.1, the push registration protocol, fixed the relay's push payload as one byte string, `{ "scp": 1 }`, while ADR-025, the Apple platform adapter, fixed the APNs payload as `{"aps": {"content-available": 1}}`. Both texts claimed to define the exact bytes the relay sends to APNs, and iOS wakes a background app only for a payload that carries `aps.content-available`, so the §10.7.1 text was wrong for APNs. ADR-027, the Android platform adapter, gave the FCM sender a body that addressed the device through the legacy FCM API's top-level `to` field, which the FCM HTTP v1 API rejects. ADR-025 acceptance criterion 4 also made `handleNotification` compare raw bytes, which no code on the iOS delivery path can run, because iOS hands the app a parsed `userInfo` dictionary.

This story replaces §10.7.1 step 5 with a wake-signal table holding one request per platform (APNs and FCM; PUSH-021 adds the WebPush row) and adds a device receipt rule per platform. The plan's decisions D1, D2 and D10 govern: D1b, the device accepts an APNs wake only when the parsed dictionary has exactly the key `aps`, and `aps` has exactly `content-available` = 1; D2b, every FCM wake carries `android.priority: HIGH`; D10, the app calls the Rust core and the Rust core calls the UniFFI `PushProvider` callback. ADR-006, the in-memory platform adapter, and ADR-025 cite the §10.7.1 table rather than restating the bytes. The SCP-096 action item that asked for an encrypted context identifier in the APNs payload contradicted §10.7, which forbids any context in a push payload, so this story removes it. Doc comments in `scp-protocol`, `scp-platform` and the Kotlin Android adapter that restated `{ "scp": 1 }` or the legacy FCM body now cite the table. Swift and Kotlin code changes belong to PUSH-017 and PUSH-018.
acceptanceCriteria: §10.7.1 step 5 contains one table with the rows APNs and FCM, each giving the request body and the headers.
The string `{ "scp": 1 }` no longer appears in §10.7.1.
`git grep -n '"scp": 1' -- .docs/specs` returns nothing; §16.12.5 cites the §10.7.1 step 5 table instead of restating payload bytes.
ADR-025 acceptance criterion 4 checks a parsed dictionary and contains no "whitespace outside string literals" clause.
ADR-027 contains no `"to":` key.
ADR-006 and ADR-025 cite §10.7.1 rather than restating the bytes.
The SCP-096 action item in `.docs/prds/main.json` no longer mentions context_id.

ADR-025 and ADR-027 state the D10 call order: `push_enable(provider)` calls `registerPush()` and publishes a signed registration; `push_handle_wake(payload)` calls `handleNotification(payload)`, then runs relay catch-up under a deadline and returns `WakeOutcome`.
§10.7.1 step 5 states the APNs receipt rule (exactly the key `aps`, and `aps` exactly `content-available` = 1) and the FCM receipt rule (`scp` equals the string `"1"`).
The FCM row of the §10.7.1 table sets `android.priority` to `HIGH` and carries no `notification` key.
`python3.12 scripts/check-doc-citations.py` passes.
actionItems: Replace §10.7.1 step 5's payload sentence with the wake-signal table and the device receipt rule.
Amend ADR-025: the Decision's push paragraph, criterion 4 (parsed-dictionary rule, relay item, call order) and criterion 7's test item.
Amend ADR-027: the Decision's FCM items, the `AndroidPushProvider.kt` code block (FCM HTTP v1 body) and criterion 10 (call order).

stories.title: Amend the push encoding, freshness, relay exception and privacy statement
stories.description: Fixes the stale copies and gaps the plan's decisions D4, D6a, D7, D8 and D9 found in the push wire format. §22.11.4, the push wire table, encodes `contexts` as length-prefixed strings with no element count, while §9.5.1, which §22.11.4 cites, requires a 4-byte big-endian element count before every repeated field; §9.5.1 governs. §10.7.1 restates the registration struct with types that drifted from the §22.11.4 wire table, so §10.7.1 cites §22.11.4 instead. §9.5.2 gets one signed-structure table per push separator (`SCP-PUSH-REGISTER-V1:` and `SCP-PUSH-DEREGISTER-V1:`); both preimages end with the canonical `relay_url` under §9.5.1's length-prefixed rule, so a signature binds to one relay (D8); the V1 encoding is fixed in place without a V2 bump, because no code has ever signed with V1 (D4b). §9.18.2 registers the reserved routing derivation `SHA-256("scp-push-registration" || relay_url)` and the canonical form of `relay_url`. §9.5.2 lists both push messages among the preimages that take an identity identifier: the `registrant` field is encoded as the 56-byte `scp:` text form of the SCP-308 S1 `Identifier` under §9.5.1's length-prefixed rule, and the separators stay V1 when S1 changes the bytes inside the length prefix. ADR-004, the native relay protocol, lists push interception as a second narrow exception to relay opacity, registers the push wire codes, the timestamp skew window, and the rule that the relay never stores or delivers a push message as a blob. The §10.7.1 storage paragraph states that a relay holding a push registration learns the identity, its platform token and the routing IDs listed for it (D7), and §9.10.4 lists that linkage as a residual. §17.17, capability selection, and the ADR-062 classification table add rows for the push registration store (shipped arm SQLite only; the in-memory arm compiles only under `testing`), the push senders, and the push signature verifier.

§9.5.2 has one table per push separator.

Both §9.5.2 push preimages end with the canonical `relay_url` as a 4-byte big-endian length and its UTF-8 bytes, and §22.11.4 and §10.7.1 state that the relay verifies against its own canonical URL, so a message signed for a different relay URL fails verification and gets 4060.

§9.18.2 registers the reserved routing derivation and the canonical form of `relay_url` (indicator: the WebSocket URL the client dialed, scheme and host lowercased, default port elided, no trailing slash).
§10.7.1 cites §22.11.4 rather than restating the struct.
ADR-004 lists two narrow exceptions, the codes 4060-4064 and 5003-5004, the skew window, and the rule that push messages are never stored or delivered as blobs.
ADR-004 states that a relay whose push role is `Disabled` rejects any PUBLISH to the reserved routing ID with code 4063.
The §10.7.1 storage paragraph states the D7 linkage, and §9.10.4 lists it as a residual.

§17.17 and the ADR-062 table each have rows for the push store, the push senders and the push verifier, each with its classification; the push store row states that the shipped arm is SQLite and the in-memory arm compiles only under `testing`.
`python3.12 scripts/check-doc-citations.py` passes.
actionItems: Add the element count to §22.11.4 and replace §10.7.1's struct with a citation of §22.11.4.
Add the two §9.5.2 tables and the §9.18.2 registration.
Amend ADR-004 with the second exception, the wire codes, the skew window and the no-blob rule.

stories.title: Routing IDs, a per-device registration key, and the registrant field
stories.description: Applies Alec's 2026-10-12 rulings on D5 and D6, and keri's ruling on the identity field. D5: §10.7.1 carries plaintext `contexts: Vec<ContextId>`, which hands the relay the context ID that §9.10.4 forbids it to learn; the registration carries `routing_ids: Vec<[u8; 32]>` instead, and an empty list is invalid. D6: §10.7.1 keys a registration by identity and platform, so a second device on the same platform replaces the first, while §10.8.1 gives each device its own MLS leaf; a registration is keyed by (identity identifier, platform, token), `PushDeregistration` carries `token`, and the relay caps the registrations per identity identifier. Identity field: both messages name the signer `registrant`, typed `Identifier` as SCP-308 S1 defines it, and every text this story writes calls it the identity identifier. Alec ruled on D3 (WebPush) to specify it fully in a later gate; PUSH-021 writes that spec text, so this story leaves the WebPush enum entry and tag `0x03` as they are.
acceptanceCriteria: §22.11.4 lists `routing_ids` with a fixed 32-byte element type, and states that an empty list is invalid.
The §22.11.4 tables of both messages name the signer field `registrant: Identifier`, citing SCP-308 S1, and `registrant` is the only identity field in either table.
`PushDeregistration` contains `token` in its table and its preimage.
§10.7.1 states the (identity identifier, platform, token) registration key and the per-identity cap (indicator: 16).
§10.7.1 no longer contains `contexts: Vec<ContextId>`.
`python3.12 scripts/check-doc-citations.py` passes.
actionItems: Replace `contexts` with `routing_ids` in §22.11.4 and §10.7.1.
Rename the signer field to `registrant: Identifier` and add `token` to `PushDeregistration`.
State the registration key and the per-identity cap in §10.7.1.

stories.title: Push wire types, canonical signing bytes and test vectors
stories.description: Fixes the `PushRegistration` and `PushDeregistration` field types to match the §22.11.4 wire table, and adds the one canonical-bytes function per message, which takes the canonical relay URL the preimage ends with (§9.5.2), the MessagePack encoding, and the reserved routing ID derivation. The keri workstream's verifier computes each preimage through these canonical-bytes functions, so no other code builds a push preimage. Both messages carry the signer in `registrant`. Until SCP-308 S1 lands the `Identifier` type, `registrant` holds today's did:dht string; the code lags the spec here, and the field's doc comment and this story's PR body record that gap. When S1 lands, the bytes inside the `registrant` length prefix change and the separators stay V1. The `crates/scp-core/src/lib.rs` re-export already exists; this story checks it. Protocol types only, so every integration-checklist row is n/a.
acceptanceCriteria: `push_registration_signing_bytes` and `push_deregistration_signing_bytes` each take the relay URL as a parameter, end the preimage with its canonical form under §9.5.1's length-prefixed rule, and produce bytes equal to golden vectors checked into `test_vectors.rs`.

A golden-vector case builds the preimage of one message for two relay URLs and shows that the two preimages differ; a second case shows that `WSS://Relay.Example:443/` and `wss://relay.example` yield one preimage.
These two functions are the only code that builds a push preimage: the PUSH-005 verifier interface and the PUSH-014 registrar both call them.
A test proves that two registrations whose routing-ID lists differ only in how elements split across the list produce different preimages.
`push_registration_routing_id("WSS://Relay.Example:443/")` equals the derivation for `wss://relay.example`.
Decoding a registration with zero routing IDs returns a typed error.
`PushRegistration` carries `routing_ids: Vec<[u8; 32]>` and `registrant`, `PushDeregistration` carries `registrant` and `token`, and `registrant` is the only identity field in either struct.
The `registrant` doc comment states that the field holds today's did:dht string until SCP-308 S1, and that S1 changes the bytes inside its length prefix without a separator bump.
The `Ed25519Signature` alias is gone.

stories.title: Push signature verifier trait and refusing stub (shared with keri)
stories.description:
Lands the push verifier interface that the keri workstream implements. keri's five constraints bind: (1) the verifier is an async trait object the relay receives by injection (`Arc<dyn PushSignatureVerifier>`, ADR-062); (2) `verify` takes the typed `PushRegistration` or `PushDeregistration`, never raw signed bytes, and computes the preimage through the PUSH-004 canonical-bytes function; (3) `verify` returns `Ok` carrying the verified identifier, typed `Identifier` (SCP-308 S1; today's did:dht string until S1 lands), or one of five rejections: identifier unresolvable, key state unavailable (retryable), signature invalid, key not `Current` in `#active`, and malformed; (4) no allow-all verifier exists, even behind `testing`; (5) keri builds its verifier body after its identifier story and the §9.7.4.2 R2, R3 and R8 key-state resolution land.

Before keri lands, the production struct `KelPushVerifier` refuses every message with a sixth error, verifier unavailable, which keri's body never returns; startup wires this struct whenever push is enabled, so every relay answers 5003 and accepts nothing unverified. keri has no story ID yet, so the stub carries `// Stub — see PUSH-005`, the form `.docs/standards/sdk-common.md` §Stub and Placeholder Policy requires; when keri files the story that replaces the stub body, the comment names that story instead. Tests use a verifier that checks a real P-256 signature against a key the test supplies. The relay maps each rejection to one wire code of ADR-004's push table (PUSH-002): identifier unresolvable, signature invalid, key not Current in #active, and malformed map to 4060; key state unavailable, and a verifier call that exceeds its timeout (indicator: 10 s), map to 5004; verifier unavailable maps to 5003. Location `crates/scp-identity/src/push_verify.rs` is an indicator. keri reviews this PR and agrees to the signature before it merges.
acceptanceCriteria: `PushSignatureVerifier::verify` takes a typed `PushRegistration` or `PushDeregistration` and no byte-slice preimage parameter.

`verify` returns `Ok` carrying the verified identifier, or a `PushVerifyError` with exactly these rejections: identifier unresolvable, key state unavailable, signature invalid, key not `Current` in `#active`, malformed, and the stub-only verifier unavailable.
`KelPushVerifier::verify` returns `Err(VerifierUnavailable)` for every input, and the stub carries a `// Stub — see PUSH-005` comment.
The tests use a verifier that checks a real P-256 signature against a key the test supplies, and that verifier lives behind `testing`.
That test verifier returns `SignatureInvalid` for a message signed by a key other than the one the test supplied.
No verifier that returns `Ok` without checking a signature exists in any build, `testing` included.
A function maps each `PushVerifyError` to its wire code (4060, 5003 or 5004), and a test covers every variant.
`scripts/check-shipped-feature-graph.sh` passes unchanged.
actionItems: Write the trait, the error enum and the stub struct.
Write the signature-checking test verifier under `testing`.
Write the error-to-wire-code mapping.
Get keri's agreement on the signature before merge.

stories.title: Relay interception of push registration and deregistration
stories.description: Adds `RelayConfig.push: PushRole` with the variants `Disabled` and `Enabled(PushServiceConfig)`. `Disabled` is the default, because it fails safe in the same way as `BridgeRole::Disabled` (ADR-052, the unified construction pattern, M2 and M4). `PushServiceConfig` holds the store, the `Arc<dyn PushSignatureVerifier>` and the configured senders; all three are required, with no defaults. `RelayConfig.relay_url` is a required `LiveRelayUrl` handle holding the relay's §9.18.2 canonical URL, from which the relay derives its reserved push routing ID and rebuilds every preimage (§10.7.1 steps 2 and 3). `RelayConfig` has no `Default` (M4 fires on `relay_url`), so no relay is built without a URL. A full node seeds the handle from its domain or its NAT tier address, and the NAT-tier task sets it before republishing on a tier change; the handle keeps a bounded list of retired routing IDs, and a PUBLISH to one is refused and never stored. The push gate runs in the PUBLISH handler of every relay transport that stores blobs (WebSocket, QUIC, UDP/DTLS and WebTransport) beside `did_slots.gate_publish`, after the rate-limit, size and TTL checks and before `storage.store`; the QUIC and WebTransport configurations carry clones of the same `relay_url` handle and the same `push` field, so every listener reads one URL and a change moves all of them at once. On any verifier rejection the relay stores nothing and changes nothing. File location `push_gate.rs` is an indicator. The operation is relay-internal and has no client dispatch, so the `pw` row is n/a.
acceptanceCriteria: A PUBLISH to the reserved routing ID never reaches `storage.store` or `deliver_to_subscribers`, whatever the result; tests prove this by querying and subscribing to the reserved routing ID afterwards.
A relay with `Disabled` returns 4063.

A relay wired with that test verifier returns 4060 for a registration signed by another key and stores nothing.
A relay returns 4062 for a timestamp outside the skew window (indicator: ±300 s) or not newer than the stored one.
A relay returns 4061 for a platform with no configured sender.
A valid deregistration removes exactly its own key.
The new codes are constants in `crates/scp-relay-client/src/error.rs`.

Every listener (WebSocket, QUIC, UDP/DTLS, WebTransport) reads the shared relay URL handle: after a URL change it intercepts the new reserved routing ID and refuses the previous one, storing nothing at either; a full node's NAT tier change moves the handle.

stories.title: Push sender seam, dispatcher, and deregistration after invalid-token failures
stories.description: The `PushSender` enum has the arms `Apns`, `Fcm` and, under `testing` only, `Recording`; a recording sender reports deliveries that never happened, so it is a nullifier and must stay out of the shipped feature graph. Each `send` returns `Delivered`, `InvalidToken`, `Transient` or `ConfigError`. After `storage.store` succeeds in `handle_publish`, the relay looks up the registrations for the publish's routing ID and queues one job per token on a bounded queue (indicator: 10,000); the publish never waits on a send. A background task drains the queue. Only `InvalidToken` counts toward the 3 consecutive failures of §10.7.1; `Delivered` resets the counter, and at 3 the relay removes the registration. Tests register through the signature-checking test verifier of PUSH-005, which checks a real P-256 signature against a key the test supplies and compiles only under `testing`. File location `push_dispatch.rs` is an indicator.
acceptanceCriteria: A publish to a registered routing ID enqueues exactly one job per matching token.
A full queue drops the job, increments a counter, and the publish still succeeds.
Three `InvalidToken` outcomes in a row remove the registration.
`InvalidToken`, `InvalidToken`, `Delivered`, `InvalidToken` leaves the registration in place.
`Transient` and `ConfigError` never change the counter.

Every test registration goes through the signature-checking test verifier of PUSH-005, which checks a real P-256 signature against a key the test supplies and compiles only under `testing`.

stories.title: Rate limit of one push per 30 s per token
stories.description: §10.7.1 step 6 requires at most one push per 30 seconds per device token. The limiter keys entries by SHA-256 of the token, so no second map holds plaintext tokens. A push suppressed inside the window is dropped, not deferred, because the device pulls every pending envelope on its next wake (§10.7). The relay prunes expired entries.

stories.title: APNs sender
stories.description: Sends the APNs row of the §10.7.1 step 5 wake-signal table over HTTP/2 to `api.push.apple.com`, or to `api.sandbox.push.apple.com` when the configured environment is `sandbox`. Authenticates with an ES256 provider JWT signed by the .p8 key through the `p256` crate the workspace already uses, carrying the key ID and team ID, refreshed every 50 minutes (indicator). Response mapping: 200 to `Delivered`; 410, or 400 with reason `BadDeviceToken`, to `InvalidToken`; 403 `InvalidProviderToken` or `ExpiredProviderToken` refreshes the JWT once, then `ConfigError`; 429 or 5xx to `Transient`; `DeviceTokenNotForTopic` to `InvalidToken`; `TopicDisallowed` to `ConfigError`. stories.title: Relay push startup selection and credentials
stories.description: Implements Part 5 of the plan: push selection is mandatory, has no default, and every failure is typed and fails closed (§17.17). The variable names are indicators; the rules are the contract. `SCP_RELAY_PUSH_PLATFORMS` takes `none`, `apns`, `fcm` or `apns,fcm`; `none` sets `PushRole::Disabled`. `SCP_RELAY_PUSH_STORE` has no default and is required whenever the platform list is not `none`; a shipped build accepts only `sqlite`, because the in-memory store arm compiles only under `testing` (PUSH-006). APNs needs `SCP_RELAY_APNS_KEY_PATH`, `SCP_RELAY_APNS_KEY_ID`, `SCP_RELAY_APNS_TEAM_ID`, `SCP_RELAY_APNS_TOPIC` and `SCP_RELAY_APNS_ENVIRONMENT` (`production` or `sandbox`, no default). FCM needs `SCP_RELAY_FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_PATH`, and `SCP_RELAY_FCM_PROJECT_ID` or the JSON's `project_id`. Credentials load only from file paths; key bytes, JWTs and access tokens live in zeroizing buffers; no `Debug` implementation prints them. The ADR-004 operator table records that APNs credentials bind a relay to one Apple team and topic, and FCM credentials to one Firebase project. The `scp-node` embedded relay takes the same selection through its builder, defaulting to `Disabled` and never reading credentials implicitly; the `scp-node` file path is an indicator.
acceptanceCriteria: When `SCP_RELAY_PUSH_PLATFORMS` is unset, `start_relay_from_env` returns a typed `StartupError` with an SCP-CAPSEL code.
The value `none` yields `PushRole::Disabled`.
With `apns` listed, each missing APNs variable yields its own `StartupError` variant naming that variable.
An unreadable key file, or one with group or world permissions, yields a typed error.
The same rules hold for FCM.
`SCP_RELAY_PUSH_STORE` has no default; a shipped build accepts `sqlite` and returns a typed `StartupError` for any other value, `memory` included.
When push is enabled, the relay wires `KelPushVerifier`.
A test checks that the `Debug` output of the push config struct contains no key byte, JWT or access token.
The `scp-node` builder exposes push as an explicit selection whose default is `Disabled`.
actionItems: Parse the push variables in `startup.rs` with one typed error per failure.
Load credentials from files into zeroizing buffers.
Add the ADR-004 operator table rows and the README section.
Expose the selection in the `scp-node` builder.

stories.title: Supervisor query for push routing IDs
stories.description: `Supervisor::push_routing_ids()` fans a query out to each standing context actor. Each actor returns its `context_routing_id` and this device's current `pseudonym_routing_id` (§9.10.4). The Supervisor groups the results by canonical relay URL (§9.18.2). FFI, SDK and matrix rows are covered by PUSH-015.
acceptanceCriteria: With two contexts on two relays, the result maps each relay to exactly the routing IDs of the contexts on it.
the result contains this device's current local pseudonym routing ID for each context; after the local pseudonym changes, the next query returns the new one and not the old one
The query runs `dispatch_push_command` → actor mailbox → `handlers/push.rs` → `push_helpers.rs`.
`pipeline_wiring.rs` asserts that step.
actionItems: Add the handler and helper, and the Supervisor fan-out.
Add the `pipeline_wiring.rs` assertion.

stories.title: Runtime push registrar (build, sign, publish, deregister)
stories.description: `register(platform, token)` gets the routing IDs from PUSH-013, then for each relay builds a registration, computes its preimage through the PUSH-004 canonical-bytes function with that relay's canonical URL, and signs it with the `#active` key handle through `KeyCustody::sign`. It publishes to that relay's reserved routing ID and returns per-relay results. `deregister(platform, token)` mirrors it. The registrar re-registers when the routing-ID set changes on context join and context leave. PUSH-029, re-registration on pseudonym rotation, adds the rotation trigger. It maps wire codes to typed `PushError` values; 5003 and 5004 are retryable, 4060-4064 are not. Tests run against relays wired with the signature-checking test verifier of PUSH-005, which checks a real P-256 signature against a key the test supplies and compiles only under `testing`. Module location `push/mod.rs` is an indicator.
acceptanceCriteria: Against a relay wired with the signature-checking test verifier of PUSH-005, which checks a real P-256 signature against a key the test supplies and compiles only under `testing` and the device's `#active` public key, `register` stores one registration per relay.

`register` signs one message per relay, each over that relay's canonical URL; a test with two relays shows that the two signed preimages differ and that each relay rejects the other relay's message with 4060.
Against a relay wired with `KelPushVerifier`, `register` returns `PushError::VerifierUnavailable` for each relay.
Joining a context triggers exactly one re-registration on the affected relay.
The signed bytes contain no context ID (D7); a test checks the preimage against the context ID bytes.
`pipeline_wiring.rs` has a step assertion for `push.register`, from the registrar down to the relay PUBLISH.
actionItems: Write the registrar and its re-registration triggers.
Map the wire codes to `PushError`.
Add the `pipeline_wiring.rs` assertion.

stories.title: FFI exports push_enable, push_disable and push_handle_wake
stories.description: Implements the call order ADR-025 criterion 4 and ADR-027 criterion 10 state. UniFFI: `push_enable(provider: PushProvider, platform)` calls `register_push()` and then the PUSH-014 registrar; `push_disable` deregisters; `push_handle_wake(payload)` calls `handle_notification`, checks the wake bytes, runs PUSH-016, and returns `WakeOutcome`. napi and Python hosts have no callback provider, so they export `push_register(platform, token)`, `push_deregister` and `push_handle_wake`, taking the token directly. Adding pipeline assertions and matrix rows only adds enforcement, which AGENTS.md allows. SDK wrappers are PUSH-017, PUSH-018 and PUSH-020.
acceptanceCriteria: Each of the three bridges exports the operations.
`pipeline_wiring.rs` asserts that each export reaches the registrar.
The matrix has a `Push` domain with `register`, `deregister` and `handle_wake` rows.
A UniFFI test with a Rust-side fake provider under `testing` proves that `push_enable` calls `register_push` exactly once.
actionItems: Write the shared push module in `scp-ffi/common` and the three bridge exports.
Add the pipeline assertions, the conformance entries and the matrix rows.

stories.title: Device wake handling (connect and pull)
stories.description: On a valid wake, calls `reconnect_transport_if_pending`, then `reconnect_contexts` (or `reconnect_contexts_no_drain`) for every standing context, feeding in the last relay contacts the bridge already stores, under a 25-second deadline (ADR-025 criterion 4). The outcome is `NewData` when catch-up delivered at least one envelope, `NoData` when it delivered none, and `Failed` on a deadline expiry or error. The wake path sends no cover traffic (§9.10.6). Reuses the reconnect path the Supervisor already wires (ADR-029, offline and sync).
acceptanceCriteria: With one envelope buffered on a test relay, `push_handle_wake` returns `NewData`, and the envelope appears in the context's receive buffer.
With none buffered, it returns `NoData`.
With the relay unreachable, it returns `Failed` within the deadline plus 1 s.
An invalid payload returns a typed error and makes no relay connection.
`pipeline_wiring.rs` has a step assertion for `push.handle_wake` → `reconnect_contexts`.
actionItems: Write the wake handler over the reconnect path, with the deadline and the outcome mapping.

stories.title: Swift push provider conformance and platform adapter
stories.description: `ApplePushProvider` conforms to the UniFFI `PushProvider` protocol and throws only `ScpError`. `handleNotification` applies the parsed-dictionary rule of ADR-025 criterion 4 (amended by PUSH-001) in place of its byte comparison. The SDK gives the app `Scp.handleRemoteNotification(userInfo) async -> UIBackgroundFetchResult`, which serializes `userInfo` to JSON and calls `push_handle_wake`. Adds `ApplePlatformAdapter.make()` per ADR-025 criterion 6, and corrects ADR-025's citation of `scp.udl`. The SDK wrapper file path is an indicator. Push does not depend on `AppleStorage`, so `AppleStorage`'s conformance gap stays outside this story.
acceptanceCriteria: `ApplePushProvider` declares the UniFFI protocol conformance.
A test passing a `userInfo` with an extra `alert` key gets a thrown `ScpError`.
A test passing exactly the APNs wake dictionary gets the wake bytes.
`ApplePlatformAdapter.make()` exists and passes a provider to `push_enable`.
SwiftLint passes.
actionItems: Conform `ApplePushProvider` to `PushProvider` and replace the byte check with the parsed-dictionary rule.
Add `Scp.handleRemoteNotification` and `ApplePlatformAdapter.make()`.

stories.title: Kotlin push provider conformance and platform adapter wiring
stories.description: `AndroidPushProvider` implements the UniFFI `PushProvider` interface, following the pattern in `UniffiKeyCustody.kt`. `AndroidPlatformAdapter.make(context)` passes the provider to `push_enable`. The SDK gives the app `Scp.onMessageReceived(data: Map<String,String>)`, which serializes the data map to JSON and runs `push_handle_wake` in an expedited WorkManager job (indicator). PUSH-001 already replaced the legacy FCM body comment in `AndroidPushProvider.kt`. The SDK wrapper file path is an indicator. Push does not depend on the other Android adapters, so their conformance gaps stay outside this story.
acceptanceCriteria: `AndroidPushProvider` implements the UniFFI interface.

A data map without `scp` and a data map whose `scp` value is not `"1"` both raise SCP-TRANS-5080 (the invalid wake payload code PUSH-019 registers), and the message names which of the two cases occurred.
`make(context)` calls `push_enable` exactly once.
The Kotlin mutable-globals check passes.
actionItems: Implement the UniFFI `PushProvider` in `AndroidPushProvider`.
Wire `make(context)` and `Scp.onMessageReceived`.

stories.title: Push error codes
stories.description: `platform_error_code` maps every push failure to `SCP-CRYPTO-4060`, a code that names no push condition. This story registers push codes in `sdk-common.md` and maps each push failure to its own code. Attestation and unsupported failures, which the same function also maps to that code, get their own codes in the same PR.
acceptanceCriteria: `platform_error_code` returns registered push codes for push failures, and never `SCP-CRYPTO-4060`.
Each push code has a row in `sdk-common.md`.
Codes exist for: wake payload invalid, registration rejected, verifier unavailable, platform unavailable, and provider failure.
Attestation and unsupported failures get their own codes in the same PR.
actionItems: Register the codes and rewrite the mapping.

stories.title: Python and TypeScript push SDK wrappers
stories.description: Wraps the napi and Python exports of PUSH-015 in each SDK, with typed errors, and sets the Python and TypeScript cells of the `Push` matrix rows to true. Module paths are indicators.
acceptanceCriteria: Both SDKs expose `register`, `deregister` and `handleWake` with typed errors.
`scripts/check-sdk-coverage.py` passes with the matrix rows set to true.
actionItems: Write the two wrappers and flip the matrix cells.

stories.title: Specify the WebPush wake signal, token encoding and VAPID key publication
stories.description:
Alec ruled on 2026-10-12 (D3) that WebPush is specified fully, in its own gate after APNs and FCM. §10.7.1 lists `WebPush` in the platform enum and §22.11.4 gives it tag `0x03`, but no artifact defines its token, its request, or its receipt rule. A push service delivers a WebPush message only under RFC 8291 message encryption and RFC 8292 VAPID, so the token must carry the subscription's endpoint URL, its `p256dh` public key and its `auth` secret, and the relay must hold a VAPID key pair whose public key the browser passes to `PushManager.subscribe` as `applicationServerKey`.

This story writes the spec text. (1) §22.11.4 gives the WebPush token one canonical encoding: the endpoint as a length-prefixed UTF-8 `https` URL under §9.5.1, then `p256dh` as the 65-byte uncompressed P-256 point, then `auth` as 16 bytes; the endpoint length cap is an indicator (2048 bytes). (2) The §10.7.1 step 5 table gains a WebPush row: `POST <endpoint>` with headers `Content-Encoding: aes128gcm`, `Urgency: high`, `TTL` (indicator: 3600) and `Authorization: vapid t=<JWT>, k=<VAPID public key, base64url>`; the body is the RFC 8291 encryption of the plaintext `{"scp":"1"}` as one aes128gcm record with a fresh ephemeral key and salt per message. The VAPID JWT is ES256 with `aud` set to the endpoint's origin, `exp` at most 24 hours ahead, and `sub` set to the operator contact. (3) The device receipt rule: the decrypted data parses as a JSON object with exactly the key `scp`, whose value is the string `"1"`. (4) Browsers require `userVisibleOnly: true`, so the service worker shows a notification for every push; §10.7.1 fixes that notification's text as a constant that carries no sender, context, count or preview, which keeps §10.7's opacity. (5) A browser `PushSubscription` is bound to one `applicationServerKey`, and each relay has its own VAPID key, so §10.7.1 states how a browser with contexts on several relays holds one subscription per relay (indicator: one service-worker registration per relay, each with its own scope). (6) ADR-004 states where a relay publishes its VAPID public key (indicator: a field of the relay's handshake response) and that a relay without a VAPID key rejects a WebPush registration with 4061. (7) The endpoint is chosen by the registrant, so ADR-004 requires the relay to refuse any endpoint whose scheme is not `https` or whose host resolves to an address that is not global unicast (loopback, private, link-local, unique-local, or the relay's own addresses), with code 4060 at registration and no request sent.
acceptanceCriteria: §22.11.4 states the WebPush token encoding: length-prefixed `https` endpoint, 65-byte uncompressed `p256dh`, 16-byte `auth`, and the endpoint length cap.
The §10.7.1 step 5 table has a WebPush row giving the request line, the four headers, the VAPID JWT claims, and the encrypted body's plaintext `{"scp":"1"}` under RFC 8291 aes128gcm.

§10.7.1 step 5 states the WebPush receipt rule (a JSON object with exactly the key `scp`, whose value is the string `"1"`) and the constant notification text that carries no sender, context, count or preview.
§10.7.1 states how a browser with contexts on more than one relay holds one subscription per relay.
ADR-004 states where a relay publishes its VAPID public key, the 4061 rejection when it has none, and the endpoint refusal rule with code 4060.
The sentence "This table defines no WebPush request." is gone from §10.7.1.
`python3.12 scripts/check-doc-citations.py` passes.
actionItems: Add the WebPush token encoding to §22.11.4.
Add the WebPush row, receipt rule, notification text and per-relay subscription rule to §10.7.1.
Add the VAPID key publication and the endpoint refusal rule to ADR-004.

stories.title: WebPush sender (RFC 8291 encryption and RFC 8292 VAPID)
stories.description: Adds the `WebPush` arm of the PUSH-008 `PushSender` enum, sending the WebPush row of the §10.7.1 step 5 table (PUSH-021). Encryption follows RFC 8291: an ephemeral P-256 key pair per message, ECDH with the token's `p256dh`, the HKDF steps keyed by the token's `auth` secret, and the RFC 8188 aes128gcm content coding with a fresh 16-byte salt and one record. The VAPID JWT is ES256, signed with the relay's VAPID key through the `p256` crate the workspace already uses, and cached per endpoint origin until shortly before `exp` (indicator: 5 minutes). Before each send, the sender applies the PUSH-021 endpoint rule to the resolved address and connects to that address, so a DNS answer cannot change between the check and the request. Response mapping: 201 to `Delivered`; 404 or 410 to `InvalidToken`; 403 to `InvalidToken`, because it means the subscription was made with another `applicationServerKey`; 400, 401 or 413 to `ConfigError`; 429 or 5xx to `Transient`. Ephemeral secrets live in zeroizing buffers. End-to-end tests register through the signature-checking test verifier of PUSH-005, which checks a real P-256 signature against a key the test supplies and compiles only under `testing`. File location `push_webpush.rs` is an indicator.
acceptanceCriteria: The encryption reproduces the RFC 8291 Appendix A example: given its keys, salt and plaintext, the output equals the RFC's ciphertext byte for byte.

Against a local test server under `testing`, the request carries the four headers of the WebPush row, and the body decrypts with the test subscription's private key and `auth` secret to exactly `{"scp":"1"}`.
Two sends to one token use different ephemeral keys and salts.
The VAPID JWT's header has `alg: ES256`, and its claims have `aud` equal to the endpoint origin, `exp` at most 24 hours ahead, and `sub`.
An endpoint whose host resolves to a loopback, private, link-local or unique-local address gets no request, and a test proves it for each class.
Each response row in the description maps to its outcome.
No log line contains the endpoint, `p256dh`, `auth`, the VAPID key or the JWT; a test captures the tracing output.

Every end-to-end test registration goes through the signature-checking test verifier of PUSH-005, which checks a real P-256 signature against a key the test supplies and compiles only under `testing`.
`cargo deny` passes with any new dependency.
actionItems: Write the RFC 8291 encryption and the VAPID JWT signer.
Write the endpoint address check and connect to the checked address.
Add the `WebPush` arm to `PushSender` with the response mapping.

stories.title: Relay WebPush startup selection and VAPID key
stories.description: Extends the PUSH-012 startup rules to WebPush. The variable names are indicators; the rules are the contract. `SCP_RELAY_PUSH_PLATFORMS` accepts `webpush` in its list. With `webpush` listed, `SCP_RELAY_WEBPUSH_VAPID_KEY_PATH` (a P-256 private key file) and `SCP_RELAY_WEBPUSH_VAPID_SUBJECT` (a `mailto:` or `https:` URI) are required, with no defaults. The key loads only from a file with no group or world permissions, into a zeroizing buffer, and no `Debug` implementation prints it. The relay publishes the VAPID public key where PUSH-021 states. The ADR-004 operator table records the two variables. The `scp-node` embedded relay takes WebPush through the same explicit selection as PUSH-012, defaulting to `Disabled`; the `scp-node` file path is an indicator.
acceptanceCriteria: With `webpush` listed, each missing WebPush variable yields its own typed `StartupError` variant naming that variable.
A key file that is unreadable, has group or world permissions, or holds no P-256 private key yields a typed error.
A subject that is neither `mailto:` nor `https:` yields a typed error.
A relay started with `webpush` publishes its VAPID public key where PUSH-021 states, and a test reads it back and checks it matches the key file.
A relay started without `webpush` rejects a WebPush registration with 4061.
A test checks that the `Debug` output of the push config contains no VAPID key byte.
actionItems: Parse the WebPush variables with one typed error per failure.
Load the VAPID key and publish its public half.
Add the operator table rows, the README section and the `scp-node` selection.

sources.section: ## 17.17 Capability Selection Is Mandatory, Fails Closed, and Never Defaults
## Capability classification (§17.17.2 SCP-CAPSEL-8010 — mandatory before ship)

stories.title: Browser client WebPush subscription, registration and wake
stories.description: Gives the ADR-057 in-browser client WebPush. For each relay that holds one of its contexts, the client reads the relay's VAPID public key, subscribes with `userVisibleOnly: true` and that key under the per-relay rule of PUSH-021, encodes the subscription as the PUSH-021 token, and publishes a signed registration through the PUSH-004 canonical-bytes function, signing with the browser's own identity key (ADR-057, keys on-device). It deregisters on `pushsubscriptionchange` and re-registers with the new subscription. The service worker applies the PUSH-021 receipt rule, shows the constant notification for every accepted push, and posts the wake to each open page of the app. ADR-057 gives the browser cold presence: it participates only while a page is open. So an open page runs relay catch-up on the wake, and with no page open, catch-up runs when the user opens one. A rejected payload shows the constant notification, because the browser requires one, and causes no relay connection. Module paths are indicators.
acceptanceCriteria: With contexts on two relays, the client holds one subscription per relay, each made with that relay's VAPID public key, and one registration per relay.

The published registration's token decodes to the subscription's endpoint, `p256dh` and `auth`, and its signature verifies under the signature-checking test verifier of PUSH-005, which checks a real P-256 signature against a key the test supplies and compiles only under `testing`.
A `pushsubscriptionchange` event deregisters the old token and registers the new one.
The service worker accepts exactly `{"scp":"1"}`, and rejects a payload with an extra key, a missing `scp`, or a non-string value.
Every push, accepted or rejected, shows the same constant notification text, and a test checks that the text contains no data from the payload.
An accepted push with an open page makes that page run catch-up, and a test with one envelope buffered on a test relay sees it delivered.
The matrix `Push` rows record the TypeScript browser cells.
actionItems: Write the subscription and registration flow in the browser client.
Write the service worker push handler with the receipt rule and the constant notification.
Wire the page-side wake to catch-up and update the matrix.

stories.title: The runtime persists each context's relay set
stories.description: Each context's actor state holds the relay endpoints that host the context, the set the §5.12.3.1 `InvitationBundle` carries as `relay_urls`. The creator sets it at create, a joiner takes the bundle's `relay_urls` at join, and import and restore install the set the snapshot stored. Each path stores a URL in its §9.18.2 canonical form when it has one. PUSH-013 groups routing IDs by this set.
acceptanceCriteria: `PerContextState` holds `relay_urls`, and `ContextSnapshot` persists it with no serde default.
`Supervisor::create_context` takes the creator's relay set, and the created context holds it.
A Welcome joiner's context holds the `relay_urls` of the `InvitationBundle` it joined through.
A snapshot of a context round-trips its relay set, and import and restore install the stored set.

Create, Welcome join, import and restore store each relay URL as its §9.18.2 canonical relay URL when the URL has one, and store every other URL exactly as written (§5.12.3.1 `relay_urls`). Two spellings of one relay become one stored entry, and no relay URL fails any of the four operations.
Every FFI bridge's create passes the bridge's connected relay set; no production caller passes an empty set when a relay set exists.
actionItems: Add the field to `PerContextState` and `ContextSnapshot`, and set it on the create, join, import and restore paths.
Pass the relay set through every create caller in the runtime, the FFI bridges and the node.
Test create, join, the snapshot round trip and restore.

checklist.dispatch: existing create, join, import and restore paths

stories.title: Pseudonym rotation in the runtime: policy, actor trigger, persisted epoch, announcement and ordered receipt
stories.description: Implements the runtime half of pseudonym rotation, which §9.10.4.1 of the security-model spec (pseudonym rotation, the BLACK-001 mitigation) specifies; issue #366, the closed pseudonym-rotation feature issue, tracked it. PUSH-027, the rotation spec amendment, wrote every clause this story cites. A context opts into rotation through `ContextParams.pseudonym_rotation`, which context governance sets through `ModifyPseudonymRotationPolicy` (ADR-031, multi-admin governance models). Contexts that do not opt in keep the v1 static pseudonym of §9.10.4, as a per-context configuration choice and not a compatibility shim. The context actor owns rotation timing: an actor-owned timer arm, armed from persisted state like the TTL arm (ADR-049, the actor-per-context concurrency model, Decision 1 and A3), plus the membership-change trigger. The actor holds no signer and no KeyCustody, so the actor only signals that a rotation is due. PUSH-028, the rotation bridge story, builds the bridge-side driver that derives the new routing ID through `KeyCustody::derive_rotatable_pseudonym` and dispatches it back as `RotatePseudonym`. This story builds everything the driver dispatches into: the command, the fail-closed persist of the rotation state, the v2 announcement, the epoch-ordered receipt in `scp-runtime` and `scp-client`, the local-routing-ID query, and the `LocalPseudonymRotated` event. Bindings from keri: rotation reads no key state; any change to the key or secret that `pseudonym_secret` derives from (§9.10.4.A) (keri slice S12) changes every pseudonym, so no persisted routing ID is assumed to survive that change; native and browser pseudonyms differ by design (§9.10.4.A). Merge order: the PR that adds the rotation state to `ContextSnapshot` merges after PUSH-025 and rebases on it. PUSH-025 is a story not yet on main that changes `PerContextState` and `ContextSnapshot` through the same `build_snapshot_from_state`, `strip_snapshot_for_public` and governance-migration paths, and its field has no serde default. PUSH-025 stays out of `blockedBy` because `scripts/validate-prd.py` rejects a reference to a story that push.json does not contain. The push registrar's re-registration on rotation is PUSH-029, not this story. The DID-level membership-change classifier, and the rotation-due signal and record deletion on a processed membership Commit, are PUSH-030, the non-committing member story. Types and file locations named here (`RotatePseudonym`, `LocalRoutingIds`, `LocalPseudonymRotated`, `PseudonymRotationState`) are indicators.
acceptanceCriteria: Opt-in (§9.10.4.1 'Rotation is opt-in'): in a context created without a rotation policy, the local routing ID equals the v1 derivation (§9.10.4), and a test clock advanced past 1000 policy periods produces zero rotation signals and an unchanged routing ID.

Policy in governance (§9.10.4.1 'Rotation policy, and where it lives'): a context created with a rotation policy persists it in `ContextParams`. An executed `ModifyPseudonymRotationPolicy` that sets or changes the policy takes effect on the next actor turn and survives restore. A non-member's or unapproved proposal leaves the policy unchanged. Context creation and the action each reject a policy that sets no trigger, and a policy whose `interval_secs` is below 600 s. An executed action that sets `None` produces zero later rotation signals, and the local routing ID stays the routing ID held before the action.

Trigger in the context actor (§9.10.4.1 'Epoch schedule'): with an interval policy and a test clock, the context actor signals 'rotation due' at `T0 + j × interval_secs` for j = 1, 2, 3, where `T0` is the context's convergent creation timestamp, with no bridge or caller action. A test clock that jumps past three boundaries while the actor is stopped yields exactly one signal after restore. With `on_membership_change`, each committed AddMember or RemoveMember yields exactly one signal on every member except the added or removed member. Because the signal channel is lossy, the actor repeats the signal until the epoch advances.

Persisted epoch (§9.10.4.1 'Rotation order and crash recovery'): after `RotatePseudonym` with epoch N+1 commits, the persisted `ContextSnapshot` holds epoch N+1, the new local routing ID, the previous routing ID with its `grace_until`, and `announce_pending`. A `RotatePseudonym` whose epoch is not the persisted epoch plus one, or not the schedule index k of the 'First v2 derivation' clause for a member with no v2 epoch yet, is rejected and changes nothing. A snapshot written before this change decodes as 'no rotation state'. If the fail-closed persist fails, the epoch, local routing ID and previous routing ID stay unchanged and no announcement is sent.

Announcement (§9.10.4.1 'Announcement wire format (v2)' and 'Announcement channel'; §25.19 Vector 58): each committed rotation sends exactly one MLS application message, published only to the shared `context_routing_id`. Its plaintext is byte-equal to the Vector 58 encoding of `pseudonym_epoch = N+1` and the new routing ID, and `announce_pending` is clear after the publish succeeds.

Vector 58 (§25.19): a test in `scp-protocol` and a native plus `wasm32` test in `scp-client-wasm` reproduce both Vector 58 byte strings, and every decision and `reason` string in the Vector 58 classifier table.

Peers record the announced routing ID (§9.10.4 announcement validation; §9.10.4.A 'no member ever recomputes a peer's pseudonym'): a native peer (`scp-runtime`) and a browser peer (`scp-client`) that receive the announcement set the sender's registry record to the announced epoch and a routing ID byte-equal to the announced `routing_id`. The test uses a custody whose routing ID no peer can compute. Their next application send addresses only the new routing ID, and each emits one `ContextEvent::PseudonymAnnounced`.

Receipt ordering (§9.10.4.1 'Receipt ordering'): an announcement with the zero sentinel, the shared `context_routing_id`, the broadcast RID, a routing ID registered to another DID, or the receiver's own current or in-grace previous routing ID is rejected and leaves the registry unchanged. A v2 announcement with a lower epoch, or with an equal epoch and a different routing ID, is rejected and leaves the registry unchanged. An equal epoch with an equal routing ID changes nothing and emits no event. A v1 announcement from a DID whose record holds a v2 epoch is rejected. Committing a member's removal or departure deletes that member's record, and the member's v2 announcement at a lower epoch after rejoining is accepted. The registry epochs survive snapshot and restore.

Grace end and leave (§9.10.4.1 'Transition protocol and grace' and 'Leave, close and expiry during a grace'): when the grace arm fires, the persisted previous routing ID is cleared and the actor emits a grace-end event. Leaving, closing or expiring a context during a grace discards the grace state and disarms the rotation and grace arms.

Routing-ID query and event (needed by PUSH-029): after a rotation, `Supervisor::push_routing_ids()` (PUSH-013) holds the new pseudonym routing ID and not the old one, and `LocalRoutingIds` returns the current routing ID and the in-grace previous routing ID. The supervisor event channel carries `LocalPseudonymRotated` once per committed rotation, and that event carries no routing ID.

Runtime wiring (AGENTS.md integration checklist): rotation commits through `dispatch_command` → actor mailbox → `handlers/messaging.rs` → `messaging_helpers.rs`; the local-routing-ID query runs `dispatch_query` → `handlers/queries.rs` → `queries_helpers.rs`. `pipeline_wiring.rs` asserts both steps, and asserts that the rotation helper calls `send_pseudonym_announcement`.

stories.title: Pseudonym rotation in the bridges: rotation driver, napi dual subscription, catch-up, SDK and matrix rows
stories.description: Implements the bridge half of pseudonym rotation (§9.10.4.1 of the security-model spec), on top of the runtime half in PUSH-026. The context actor holds no KeyCustody, so a bridge-side driver in `scp-ffi-common`, modelled on `heartbeat_scheduler.rs`, holds a weak Supervisor reference, the custody, the identity key handle and a cancel token. On a 'rotation due' signal or on start, the driver reads `LocalRoutingIds`, calls `derive_rotatable_pseudonym` at the next epoch, and dispatches `RotatePseudonym`. At start it also runs the §9.10.4.1 re-derivation check for a change of the pseudonym-secret source and re-publishes a pending announcement. napi `context_subscribe_on` replaces its one-time pseudonym subscription with the routing-ID set that `LocalRoutingIds` returns, re-read on rotation and grace-end events and on a periodic tick, and spawns and tears down the driver next to the heartbeat scheduler. Reconnect catch-up covers the same set, which also changes what PUSH-016, device wake handling, pulls. UniFFI (whose `context_subscribe` is a stub) and PyO3 (which has no subscribe loop) export only the policy through `ContextParams` and the governance action, and the capability matrix records their dual-subscription rows as exemptions. Per the plan's PR split, the dual-subscription, restore-subscription and napi/matrix wiring criteria move here from PUSH-026. The custody-call, pseudonym-secret-source and destroyed-identity criteria also move here, because the driver this story builds is the only caller of the custody. Type and file names (`pseudonym_rotation_scheduler.rs`) are indicators.
acceptanceCriteria: Custody call only (§9.10.4.1 'Custody compatibility'; keri ruling): a counting custody double records exactly one `derive_rotatable_pseudonym` call per rotation, with `pseudonym_epoch` = persisted epoch + 1, and no other custody or key-state read. For identity seed 0x01×32 at epoch 1 the new routing ID equals the §25.19 Vector 30 v2 routing ID.

First v2 derivation (§9.10.4.1 'First v2 derivation, at join and when rotation is enabled'): a member that joins a context whose interval policy puts the test clock at schedule index k = 3 derives its routing ID with v2 at epoch 3. A v1 member of a live context on which governance enables rotation keeps its v1 routing ID until its next trigger, and that rotation derives v2 at the schedule index k of that moment.

Dual subscription, then drop (§9.10.4.1 'Transition protocol and grace'): from rotation until rotation time + 600 s, the napi subscribe loop holds subscriptions on both the old and the new routing ID, and a blob published to the old routing ID during the grace is delivered. Once the grace elapses, `TransportManager::unsubscribe` is called with the old routing ID, and a blob published to it afterwards is not delivered.

Restore and crash (§9.10.4.1 'Rotation order and crash recovery'): at each kill point the clause enumerates (after persist and before subscribe; after subscribe and before announce), a restore leaves the member subscribed to the new routing ID, and to the old one until its persisted `grace_until`, and the member re-publishes the announcement exactly once when `announce_pending` is set. A restore after `grace_until` subscribes only to the new routing ID.

Change of the pseudonym-secret source (§9.10.4.1 'Change of the pseudonym-secret source'; keri ruling S12): on restore, and on any change to the key or secret that `pseudonym_secret` derives from (§9.10.4.A), a member whose derivation at the persisted epoch differs from the persisted local routing ID rotates to epoch N+1, keeps the persisted routing ID subscribed for the grace, and announces. In a v1 context the member subscribes to and re-announces its new v1 routing ID. No code path treats the persisted routing ID as current without re-deriving it.

Destroyed identity (§9.10.4.A 'Destruction'): after the identity is destroyed, the driver's derive fails with key-not-found (SCP-CRYPTO-4006). The context keeps its epoch and routing ID, sends no announcement, and stays subscribed.

Leave, close and expiry (§9.10.4.1 'Leave, close and expiry during a grace'): leaving, closing or expiring a context during a grace calls `TransportManager::unsubscribe` for both the current and the previous routing ID, and stops the driver.

Reconnect catch-up (§9.10.4.1 'Reconnect catch-up'): a reconnect during a grace queries the shared `context_routing_id`, the current routing ID and the previous routing ID, and a blob stored on the previous routing ID while the member was offline is delivered.

Bridge wiring (AGENTS.md integration checklist): `pipeline_wiring.rs` asserts that the driver calls `derive_rotatable_pseudonym` and `rotate_pseudonym`, and that napi `context_subscribe_on` spawns and tears down the driver and calls `unsubscribe`. The capability matrix lists the rotation policy for every binding and records napi-only dual subscription, with exemptions for UniFFI (stub `context_subscribe`) and PyO3 (no subscribe loop). The TypeScript, Python, Kotlin and Swift SDKs expose the policy field and the policy `EventType` string.
actionItems: Add the `scp-ffi-common` rotation driver, including the re-derivation check for a change of the pseudonym-secret source and the pending re-announce at start.
Derive the first v2 routing ID at the schedule index on join in an opted-in context.
Replace the napi one-time pseudonym subscription with the `LocalRoutingIds` set, and spawn and tear down the driver from `context_subscribe_on`.
Extend reconnect catch-up in `reconnect.rs` to the current and in-grace routing IDs.
Export the policy through the UniFFI and PyO3 `ContextParams` and the governance action.
Add the SDK policy fields and `EventType` strings, the `pipeline_wiring.rs` assertions and the capability-matrix rows.

stories.title: Push registrar re-registers on pseudonym rotation
stories.description: Adds the rotation trigger to the PUSH-014 push registrar, so that a relay wakes a device for its current pseudonym routing ID after a rotation (§10.7.1 push registration; §9.10.4.1 pseudonym rotation). The registrar subscribes to `Supervisor::subscribe_events()`. On `ContextEvent::LocalPseudonymRotated`, which PUSH-026 emits once a rotation is persisted, the registrar re-runs `push_routing_ids()` and re-registers on each relay whose routing-ID set changed; a registration with the same token replaces the earlier one. A grace-end event changes nothing the registrar sends, because the registrar sends only current routing IDs. `broadcast::RecvError::Lagged` means the registrar re-queries every relay's set, because the event channel is lossy. The event carries no routing ID because the same channel feeds the webhook dispatcher. Module location `push/mod.rs` is an indicator.

A grace-end event triggers no re-registration.
After the registrar's event receiver returns `Lagged`, the registrar re-queries `push_routing_ids()` and re-registers on every relay whose set changed, and on no other relay.

stories.title: Non-committing members rotate on a processed membership Commit
stories.description: Implements the membership trigger of §9.10.4.1 of the security-model spec (pseudonym rotation, the BLACK-001 mitigation) for a member that did not commit the membership change. §9.10.4.1 'Epoch schedule' states that the member that commits an AddMember or RemoveMember rotates after it commits, and that every other member rotates when it processes the Commit that applies the change; it also states the membership-change criterion, which counts changes by DID and not by MLS leaf. A Commit is an AddMember for each DID that held no leaf before the Commit, and a RemoveMember for each DID whose last leaf the Commit removes. A Commit that adds or removes a device leaf of a DID that holds another leaf before and after the Commit is neither. A removed member does not rotate, and a Commit that applies several membership changes triggers one rotation. §9.10.4.1 'Receipt ordering', in its record-lifetime rule, also has a member that processes a RemoveMember Commit delete the removed DID's pseudonym-registry record. This story builds the DID-level classifier over the leaf sets before and after a Commit, and calls it on the path where the context actor processes an incoming Commit (`DeliverIncoming`, which merges the staged Commit), so that processing emits the rotation-due signal and deletes the record. PUSH-026, the runtime rotation story, owns the rotation-due signal's consumer, the committer's trigger, the timer arms and `RotatePseudonym`, and is blocked by this story. Types and file locations named here are indicators.
acceptanceCriteria: Non-committer trigger (§9.10.4.1 'Epoch schedule', membership trigger and membership-change criterion): in a context whose policy sets `on_membership_change`, a member that did not commit an AddMember or a RemoveMember emits exactly one rotation-due signal when it processes the Commit that applies that change, and a Commit that adds a second device leaf for a DID that already holds a leaf yields zero signals. Test: a two-node test in which node A creates the context, node B joins by Welcome, and A adds and then removes a third identity C; B emits one rotation-due signal when it processes the Commit adding C and one when it processes the Commit removing C. A Commit from A that adds a second device leaf for C's DID while C is a member yields no signal on B.

Record deletion on a processed Commit (§9.10.4.1 'Receipt ordering', record lifetime): in the same two-node test, after B processes A's Commit removing C, B's pseudonym registry holds no record for C's DID, and B accepts a v2 announcement from C at a lower epoch after C rejoins.
actionItems: Add a DID-level membership-change classifier over the leaf sets before and after a Commit: AddMember for a DID with no leaf before, RemoveMember for a DID whose last leaf the Commit removes, and neither for a device leaf of a DID that holds another leaf before and after.

Call the classifier on the incoming-Commit processing path, emit one rotation-due signal per Commit that applies at least one membership change when the policy sets `on_membership_change` and the local member is not the removed member, and delete each removed DID's registry record.
Add the two-node integration test with the Welcome join, the add and remove of C, and the extra device leaf.

stories.title: The 0xFF02 extension commits T0; members install T0 and the TTL base from it
stories.description: Implements the `creation_timestamp_secs` field of the `0xFF02` SCP Context Parameters MLS group-context extension and validation rule 9, which `05-contexts.md` §5.13.3 (context creation) specifies. Alec chose this design on 2026-10-13. The creator's `ContextCreated` leaf timestamp (`T0`) is a genesis fact, so the creator commits it in the extension, and every member installs it from the committed extension as `T0` for the pseudonym rotation schedule (`09-security-model.md` §9.10.4.1) and as the TTL-deadline base (`05-contexts.md` §5.10). No member takes it from an invitation bundle signature, a snapshot field, or its own clock. The extension commits the value because a bundle signature proves only who signed the bundle (§5.12.3.1 step 4, §5.13.3 rule 8). A false `T0` would make a joiner rotate alone, so a relay could link its subscriptions across rotations, and it would move the joiner's TTL deadline. The field is required: SCP has no users, so no transition path accepts an extension without it. TTL extensions still reach a member as `TTLExtended` leaves in the event log, and ADR-049's single-source TTL-deadline invariant keeps the persisted `ContextSnapshot.creation_timestamp_secs` as the prune-immune base, now filled from the committed extension. PUSH-026, the pseudonym rotation runtime story, needs `T0` on a Welcome joiner, so this story blocks PUSH-026. The rotation runtime itself is PUSH-026, not this story. File locations are indicators.
acceptanceCriteria: Creator writes the field (§5.13.3 'Creation timestamp'): a context created at test-clock time T0 carries a `0xFF02` extension whose JCS bytes include `creation_timestamp_secs` equal to the `timestamp` of the creator's `ContextCreated` leaf, and that value is unchanged in the extension after a later AddMember Commit. Creation rejects a creation timestamp above 2^53 − 1.

Install on join, import and restore (§5.13.3 rule 9): a Welcome joiner, an import and a restore each set the context's `T0` and its TTL-deadline base to the committed `creation_timestamp_secs`. A test whose invitation bundle, snapshot or local clock carries a different value shows the installed value still equals the committed one. The SDK rejects an import or restore whose snapshot creation timestamp differs from the committed value, before it installs any authority.

Reject a missing or invalid field (§5.13.3 rule 1 and rule 9): a Welcome join, an import and a restore each reject an MLS group whose `0xFF02` extension omits `creation_timestamp_secs`, carries a value above 2^53 − 1, or carries a value later than the member's clock plus 300 s, and each rejection installs no governance engine and no admin set.

Two-node test (§9.10.4.1 'Epoch schedule' and 'First v2 derivation'; §5.10 'Deadline base'): node A creates a context at T0 with `interval_secs` 3600 and a 5 h TTL, and node B joins through a Welcome at T0 + 3.5 h. B's first v2 epoch is 3, A and B each signal 'rotation due' at the same boundary T0 + 4 h, and B's TTL deadline is T0 + 5 h, not T0 + 8.5 h.

The two-node test above replaces the PUSH-026 test `a_welcome_joiner_admits_no_interval_rotation_without_the_creators_t0` in `spawn_from_welcome_tests.rs`, which the story deletes; a repository search for that test name returns no hit.
actionItems: Add the required `creation_timestamp_secs: u64` to the `0xFF02` extension type, its JCS serialization, and its validation, with the 2^53 − 1 bound.
Write the field at context creation from the `ContextCreated` leaf timestamp.
On Welcome join, import and restore, read `T0` and the TTL base from the committed extension, check the snapshot value against it, and apply the future bound of §9.8.2.
Replace the PUSH-026 Welcome-joiner test with the two-node test.
